You are a black-box reverse-engineering specialist. Work empirically: RUN the reference executable many
times and record exactly what it does. Never run the 'python' command; the executable is self-contained.
Be exhaustive — dozens of invocations is the expected volume. Use bash loops, printf for raw bytes,
'cat -A' / 'od -c' to make whitespace and newlines unambiguous, and check exit codes every time.


=== ORIGINAL PYTHON SOURCE (/workspace/dataset/test8.py) ===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse
import construct

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--b', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--c', type=str, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    format1 = construct.Int8ul.build(args.a)
    format2 = construct.Int8ul.build(args.b)
    length = len(args.c)
    format3 = construct.Bytes(length).build(args.c.encode())
    print(format1)
    print(format2)
    print(format3)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Reference executable: /workspace/dataset/test8_executable   (run it directly; NEVER use the 'python' command)
Program name in argparse messages is literally "test8_executable".

[stdout, success] three lines, each a Python bytes repr, each followed by \n:

[python bytes repr rules confirmed]
  quote choice: default "'"; if bytes contain "'" and NOT '"', use '"'; if both present use "'" and escape \'
    b"it's"          (only single quote)
    b'say "hi"'      (only double quote)
    b'both\'"x'      (both -> single-quoted, \' escaped)
  escapes: backslash -> \\ , \t , \n , \r  (ONLY these three control chars are named)
    other bytes < 0x20, 0x7f, and >= 0x80 -> \xNN  (lowercase hex, always 2 digits)
    verified: bell->\x07, vtab->\x0b, esc->\x1b, del->\x7f, 0x01->\x01

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ON THE GENERATED CODE ===
* Pure JavaScript, Node.js, ESM ONLY: 'import' / 'export'. require() and module.exports are FORBIDDEN.
* Every generated file uses the .mjs suffix; every relative import includes the full './x.mjs' suffix.
* ZERO npm/external dependencies. Only local relative imports and node: builtins (node:fs, node:process...).
* NEVER import, use, or even mention DataView or ArrayBuffer anywhere (comments included). This is a hard
  ban from the task statement. Use Uint8Array (build with Uint8Array.from / Uint8Array.of / new Uint8Array(len))
  or plain number arrays. Do not call .buffer on a typed array.
* No embedded Python. No child_process shelling out to python.
* Hierarchical: split the library into multiple focused modules under /output/lib/ that export their
  interfaces; the entry point /output/test8.mjs wires them together.
* Node is v18.19.1.


YOUR ASSIGNED AREA: bytes-repr

Reverse-engineer Python's BYTES REPR formatting as printed by /workspace/dataset/test8_executable on line 3 (and lines 1-2).

Line 3 prints the repr of the UTF-8 encoding of --c, but ONLY when the code-point length of --c equals its
UTF-8 byte length (otherwise you get an exit-1 StreamError). So to probe arbitrary byte values on line 3 use
pure-ASCII/Latin-1-safe inputs where those lengths coincide; to probe HIGH bytes (0x80-0xff) use lines 1 and 2
instead via --a/--b (e.g. --a 128 prints repr of a single byte 0x80).

Determine for EVERY byte 0x00..0xff how it renders inside the repr. Drive lines 1 and 2 across all 256 values
with a loop and record the output. Then determine quote selection and escaping on multi-byte strings via --c:
no quotes present; only "'"; only '"'; both; backslashes; tab/newline/CR; other C0 controls; DEL.
Confirm whether \a \b \f \v \0 are ever emitted as named escapes or always as \xNN.
Confirm hex case and zero padding. Confirm the 'b' prefix and absence of spaces.

Deliver a complete, exact byte -> rendering table (summarized by ranges where identical) and the precise
quote-selection algorithm.

Do not write any files under /output. Your job is purely to establish truth.

rules.rule: Output shape: exactly three lines on stdout, each a Python bytes repr followed by a single \n (0x0A). No trailing spaces, no extra blank line, no line wrapping/truncation at any length. Line1 = repr of the 1-byte encoding of --a, Line2 = repr of the 1-byte encoding of --b, Line3 = repr of the UTF-8 bytes of --c. All three use the IDENTICAL repr algorithm.
rules.evidence:
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 39 --b 34 --c "it's" | od -c
0000000   b   "   '   "  \n   b   '   "   '  \n   b   "   i   t   '   s
0000020   "  \n
0000022
EXIT=0

rules.rule: Prefix is a single lowercase ASCII 'b' immediately followed by the opening quote — no space anywhere (not after b, not inside).

QUOTE SELECTION (computed once over the WHOLE byte sequence, before any escaping): let hasSQ = sequence contains byte 0x27 ('), hasDQ = sequence contains byte 0x22 ("). If (hasSQ && !hasDQ) the delimiter is '"' (double quote); in EVERY other case (no quotes at all, only ", or both) the delimiter is "'" (single quote). Empty sequence -> single quote -> b''.
rules.evidence:
$ for c in "abc" "it's" 'say "hi"' "both'\"x" "'" '"' "'''" "'''\"" ""; do /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c "$c" | sed -n 3p; done
b'abc'
b"it's"
b'say "hi"'
b'both\'"x'
b"'"
b'"'
b"'''"
b'\'\'\'"'
b''

rules.rule: ESCAPING is strictly per-byte and independent of position/order. Per byte c, in priority order: (1) if c==0x27 AND delimiter is "'" -> emit \' (backslash + apostrophe); (2) if c==0x5c -> emit \\ (two backslashes); (3) if c==0x09 -> \t ; c==0x0a -> \n ; c==0x0d -> \r ; (4) if c<0x20 or c>=0x7f -> \xNN ; (5) otherwise (0x20..0x7e) emit the raw ASCII character. Note byte 0x22 (") is NEVER escaped: when the delimiter is "'" it is emitted literally, and the delimiter can only be '"' when no 0x22 is present, so a \" escape is unreachable.
rules.evidence:
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c "both'\"x" | od -c
0000020   b   '   b   o   t   h   \   '   "   x   '  \n
EXIT=0
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c "a\\b'c" | sed -n 3p | cat -A
b"a\\b'c"$

rules.rule: Byte 0x5c (backslash) is doubled to \\ regardless of which delimiter was chosen (including inside a double-quoted repr).
rules.evidence:
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c "a\\b'c" | sed -n 3p | cat -A
b"a\\b'c"$
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c 'a\\b' | od -c
0000020   b   '   a   \   \   \   \   b   '  \n

rules.rule: ONLY THREE named control escapes exist: \t (0x09), \n (0x0a), \r (0x0d). Python does NOT emit \a, \b, \f, \v, \0, \e, or \0NN octal — those become \xNN.
rules.evidence:
$ for h in 07 08 0c 0b 1b 00; do ... done  (via --a)
  7	b'\x07'   (BEL, not \a)
  8	b'\x08'   (BS,  not \b)
 11	b'\x0b'   (VT,  not \v)
 12	b'\x0c'   (FF,  not \f)
 27	b'\x1b'   (ESC)
  0	b'\x00'   (NUL, not \0)
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c $'a\ab' | sed -n 3p  ->  b'a\x07b'
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c $'a\vb' | sed -n 3p  ->  b'a\x0bb'

rules.rule: \xNN form: literal backslash, literal lowercase 'x', then EXACTLY two lowercase-hex digits, always zero-padded (\x00, \x07, \x0b, \x7f, \xa0, \xff). Never uppercase (\xFF), never 1-digit (\x7), never \u/\U.

COMPLETE 0x00..0xff table (verified by driving all 256 values through --a/--b in 128 invocations): 0x00-0x08 -> \x00..\x08 ; 0x09 -> \t ; 0x0a -> \n ; 0x0b-0x0c -> \x0b,\x0c ; 0x0d -> \r ; 0x0e-0x1f -> \x0e..\x1f ; 0x20-0x21 -> literal (space, !) ; 0x22 -> literal " ; 0x23-0x26 -> literal ; 0x27 -> \' if single-quoted else literal ' ; 0x28-0x5b -> literal ; 0x5c -> \\ ; 0x5d-0x7e -> literal ; 0x7f -> \x7f ; 0x80-0xff -> \x80..\xff (all lowercase two-digit hex).
rules.evidence:
$ for i in $(seq 0 2 254); do j=$((i+1)); out=$(/workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a $i --b $j --c q); printf '%3d\t%s\n%3d\t%s\n' "$i" "$(sed -n 1p <<<"$out")" "$j" "$(sed -n 2p <<<"$out")"; done > /tmp/bytes.txt
$ node /tmp/gen.mjs > /tmp/exp2.txt && diff /tmp/exp2.txt /tmp/bytes.txt && echo MODEL_MATCHES_ALL_256
MODEL_MATCHES_ALL_256

rules.rule: Multiple occurrences of ' in a both-quotes sequence are EACH escaped (not just the first).
Order of ' and " in the sequence is irrelevant — only set membership matters.
rules.evidence:
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c "'\"" | sed -n 3p | cat -A
b'\'"'$
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c "\"'" | sed -n 3p | cat -A
b'"\''$

rules.rule: Empty --c renders as b'' (two single quotes) on line 3, exit 0.
rules.evidence:
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c '' | od -c
0000000   b   '   \   x   0   1   '  \n   b   '   \   x   0   2   '  \n
0000020   b   '   '  \n
0000024
EXIT=0

rules.rule: No length limit / no wrapping: a 285-character string of all printable ASCII repeated 3x renders as one single line.
rules.evidence:
$ LONG=$(node -e 'let s="";for(let i=32;i<127;i++)s+=String.fromCharCode(i);process.stdout.write(s.repeat(3))'); /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c "$LONG" | sed -n 3p | cat -A
b' !"#$%&\'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~ ... (repeated 3x) ...'$   (exit 0, one line, terminated by $)

rules.rule: Differential fuzz: a JS implementation of the above algorithm matched the executable on 65/65 cases (60 pseudo-random 1-10 byte strings biased toward 0x27/0x22/0x5c/0x09/0x0a/0x0d/0x07/0x0b/0x0c/0x1b/0x01/0x7f, plus empty, ', ", '\", \\').

Bytes 0x80-0xff are UNREACHABLE on line 3: --c with a non-ASCII character either trips the StreamError length check (codepoint count != UTF-8 byte count) or, for raw invalid-UTF-8 argv bytes, raises UnicodeEncodeError before construct. They are only reachable via --a/--b (lines 1-2), where they always render as \xNN.
rules.evidence:
$ /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 200 --b 240 --c q
b'\xc8'
b'\xf0'
b'q'
(exit 0)  — and every high byte 128..255 in /tmp/bytes.txt renders as \x80..\xff

gotchas: Quote selection MUST be a two-pass algorithm: scan the whole byte sequence for 0x27 and 0x22 FIRST, pick the delimiter, THEN escape. A naive single-pass that escapes as it goes cannot know the delimiter yet and will get b"it's" wrong (emitting b'it\'s').

The condition is exactly `hasSQ && !hasDQ` -> double quote. It is NOT `hasSQ -> double quote`. When BOTH are present Python uses SINGLE quotes and escapes the apostrophes: b'both\'"x'. A common wrong implementation picks double quotes whenever an apostrophe exists.

Byte 0x22 (") is never escaped. Do not add a `if (c===0x22) s += '\\"'` branch that fires when the delimiter is a double quote — it is dead code, but if you also mis-derive the delimiter it will produce wrong output. Inside single quotes, " is emitted raw.
Only \t, \n, \r are named. JS developers reflexively add \b, \f, \v, \0 (all of which JS's own escape conventions have). Python emits \x08, \x0c, \x0b, \x00 for those. Also no octal escapes.
Hex must be LOWERCASE and zero-padded to exactly 2 digits: use c.toString(16).padStart(2,'0'). `toString(16).toUpperCase()` or unpadded output (\x7 instead of \x07) both diverge.
0x7f (DEL) is escaped (\x7f) even though it is < 0x80. The printable range is 0x20..0x7e INCLUSIVE on both ends; the test must be `c >= 0x20 && c <= 0x7e`, i.e. `c < 0x20 || c >= 0x7f` -> hex.
Backslash (0x5c) is doubled regardless of the chosen delimiter, including inside double-quoted reprs: b"a\\b'c". Don't make backslash escaping conditional on the quote character.

Line 3's input is the UTF-8 byte sequence, but the program only reaches the print when codepoint-count == UTF-8-byte-count. If you build the byte array from a JS string, iterate CODE POINTS (for...of or Array.from), not .length / charCodeAt — '\u{1F600}'.length is 2 in JS but 1 in Python.

Iterate over a Uint8Array/number array of BYTES, not over JS string characters. A JS string built by latin1-decoding is fine, but a UTF-16 string indexed by charCodeAt will yield values > 255 for non-ASCII and produce \xNNN-style garbage.
Empty input renders b'' with SINGLE quotes (the hasSQ&&!hasDQ test is false), not b"".
Every escape is independent and per-byte; there is no lookahead/context (e.g. an escaped byte followed by a hex digit is not disambiguated). b'\x0141' stays as-is for bytes [0x01,'4','1'].
All three lines share one repr function — don't special-case lines 1/2 as 'always \xNN'. --a 65 prints b'A', --a 39 prints b"'", --a 92 prints b'\\'.
No space between the b prefix and the quote, and no space anywhere Python wouldn't put one. Verified byte-for-byte with od -c: bytes are 'b',0x22,0x27,0x22,0x0a.
